wave64.reason: The GPU work is inseparable from a graphics pipeline, which no wave64 part has. Velvet shares its particle position and normal buffers with OpenGL through graphics interop: VtRegisteredBuffer wraps cudaGraphicsGLRegisterBuffer over a GL vertex buffer object, and the solver reads and writes those very buffers. Every wave64 architecture is CDNA and CDNA is compute-only, so the driver refuses to create an OpenGL context there; linux-gfx90a is recorded blocked for exactly that reason and is the only wave64 host in the fleet. This is not a scheduling gap more hardware would close: no wave64 part has a graphics pipeline, so no evidence can ever exist. Meets the NARROW criterion added to config/arches.toml on 2026-08-25, not the loose one it warns against -- this is not merely a project with a GUI, nor a README claiming a graphics pipeline is needed. There is NO headless compute subset to validate instead: the device buffers ARE the graphics buffers, so the solve loop cannot be reached without a GL context. That is precisely why the earlier standalone kernel test was a smoke check rather than a validation, and why two defects survived four platform passes. Coverage that DOES exist at head a9016bc: wave32 and windows are both satisfied by windows-gfx1151, validated against the real application -- extent 2.0x2.0 held over 200 physics frames, sag 1.5 to 0.72-0.80 with corners pinned at 1.500, textured mesh rendering, zero NaN with the detector self-tested against a manufactured NaN, both interop copies returning success, and the Self Collision and High Resolution scenes exercised. The upstream PR body already states that compute-only parts cannot run this application.

linux-gfx90a.blocked_reason: compute-only CDNA2 (MI250X): no graphics pipeline, AMD driver refuses a GL context, so OpenGL<->HIP buffer interop (hipGraphicsGLRegisterBuffer) is unavailable and the cloth-sim kernels behind it cannot run; builds but is not GPU-runnable. Port validated on RDNA (gfx1100, gfx1201).
